en: to settle; to fix; to bring something to a close

examples.ko: 오늘은 이 문제를 끝까지 결판내야 해요.
examples.en: Today we have to settle this problem once and for all.
Let's not fight; let's settle it with rock-paper-scissors.
There is not enough time to settle it through negotiation.

examples.ko: 그 일은 우리가 직접 만나서 결판냈어요.
examples.en: We met in person and settled that matter.
They went to extra time to settle the match.

examples.ko: 이사장은 이번 주 안에 결판낼 생각이에요.
examples.en: The chairman plans to settle it within this week.

explain: 옳고 그름이나 이기고 지는 것을 확실하게 가려서 끝낼 때 써요. '끝내다'보다 승부를 가르는 느낌이 강하고, '결판을 내다'처럼 사이에 '을'을 넣어서도 말해요.

phrases.en: I'm definitely going to settle this today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '결판내다'를 두 말로 나눠 쓴 형태로 뜻은 같아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The same meaning, with the verb split into two parts.

phrases.en: The winner was decided in the final game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 스스로 결과가 가려졌을 때 써요. 누군가 일부러 끝낸 게 아니에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the result becomes clear on its own, not when someone ends it.

phrases.en: My friend suggested we settle it with a game.
phrases.nuance_ko: 친구끼리 반말로 승부를 제안할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual way for friends to propose settling something.

explain_en: Use it when you clearly decide right and wrong or winner and loser and bring things to an end. It has a stronger feeling of deciding the outcome than '끝내다', and you can also say it as '결판을 내다' with '을' in between.

examples.en: The kids smashed the sandcastle with their feet.
It isn't easy to smash prejudice.

examples.ko: 동생이 블록으로 쌓은 탑을 깨부수고 웃었어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling smashed the tower built of blocks and laughed.

examples.ko: 우리 선수가 세계 기록을 깨부수고 우승했어요.
examples.en: Our athlete smashed the world record and won.

examples.ko: 화가 나도 물건을 깨부수면 안 돼요.
examples.en: Even when you're angry, you must not smash things.

examples.ko: 낡은 벽을 깨부숴야 새로 지을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You have to tear down the old wall before you can build a new one.

explain: '부수다'보다 힘을 세게 줘서 때려 부수는 느낌이 있어요. '편견·기록·틀을 깨부수다'처럼 비유로도 자주 써요. 활용은 '깨부숴요, 깨부쉈어요'예요.

phrases.en: The child smashed the toy block tower.
phrases.nuance_ko: '깨부수다'의 과거형이에요. '수'와 '었'이 줄어서 '쉈'이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the past tense. '수' and '었' contract into '쉈'.

phrases.en: We smashed the old wall and built a new one.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-고'로 이어서 부순 다음에 하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-고' you can link what you did after smashing something.

phrases.en: That athlete smashed the world record.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기록'과 함께 쓰면 기록을 크게 뛰어넘었다는 비유 표현이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '기록', it figuratively means beating a record by a large margin.

explain_en: It feels more forceful than '부수다', like smashing something with strength. It is also often used figuratively, as in breaking prejudice, records or molds. The conjugation is '깨부숴요, 깨부쉈어요'.

en: to guffaw; to roar with laughter

examples.en: My friends are laughing loudly watching a cartoon.
Every time we meet, he greets me with a hearty laugh.
The boys were guffawing in the back.
Stop guffawing and tell me why.
Grandfather roared with laughter at his grandchild's antics.
I woke up to my coworkers' loud laughter.

explain: '껄껄거리다'와 같은 뜻으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 둘 다 '껄껄 웃다'를 한 동사로 만든 말이고, 크게 웃는 소리가 계속 들릴 때 써요. 윗사람이 웃으면 '껄껄대셨어요'처럼 높여요.

phrases.en: Grandfather heard the joke and laughed heartily.
phrases.nuance_ko: '껄껄대다'와 뜻이 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the same as 껄껄대다, so you can swap them.

phrases.en: My friends talked while roaring with laughter, so the classroom was noisy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃으면서 말하는 모습을 한 문장으로 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to describe talking while laughing loudly, joining the two actions.

phrases.en: Grandfather heard that story and guffawed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 윗사람이 크게 웃을 때 '-시-'를 넣어 높여 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-시-' to show respect when an elder laughs loudly.

explain_en: It can replace '껄껄거리다' with the same meaning. Both turn '껄껄 웃다' into one verb for loud laughter that keeps going. For someone senior, use the honorific, like '껄껄대셨어요'.

examples.ko: 강아지가 배가 고픈지 낑낑거리는 소리를 내요.
examples.en: The puppy makes whining sounds, maybe because it's hungry.
I struggled and groaned while carrying the heavy box.
The child is straining to open the drawer.

examples.ko: 문제를 풀려고 혼자 낑낑거리지 말고 질문하세요.
examples.en: Don't struggle over the problem alone. Ask a question.

examples.ko: 강아지가 문 앞에서 낑낑거려서 나가 봤어요.
examples.en: The puppy was whining at the door, so I went out to look.
I saw a bicycle struggling up the hill.

explain: 강아지가 낑낑 우는 소리도 되고, 사람이 힘든 일을 하느라 애쓰는 모습도 돼요. 아프거나 고민으로 앓는 느낌의 '끙끙거리다'와 달리 힘을 쓰거나 강아지가 칭얼거리는 모습에 더 어울려요.

phrases.en: The puppy whimpers in front of the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: '낑낑거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 입말에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly identical to 낑낑거리다, common in speech.

phrases.en: Grandma lifted the heavy bag, grunting with effort.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-며'로 힘들게 하는 동작과 이어서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Connected with '-며' to the strained action.

phrases.en: Don't struggle on your own, give it to me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘들게 혼자 애쓰는 사람에게 도와주겠다고 할 때 쓰는 존댓말 부정 명령이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite negative command used when offering help to someone struggling alone.

explain_en: It can describe a puppy's whining sound, and also a person straining over something hard. Unlike '끙끙거리다', which suggests suffering from pain or worry, it fits better with physical effort or a puppy whimpering.

examples.ko: 그는 화가 나서 문을 냅다 걷어찼어요.
examples.en: He was angry and kicked the door hard.

examples.ko: 비가 오자 아이들이 집으로 냅다 뛰어갔어요.
examples.en: When the rain started, the kids dashed home at full speed.

examples.ko: 친구가 공을 냅다 던지는 바람에 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: My friend hurled the ball so hard that I was startled.

examples.ko: 소리를 냅다 지르고 나니 속이 시원했어요.
examples.en: After I yelled at the top of my lungs, I felt relieved.
A dog suddenly came charging at me, so I ran away.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말도 없이 내 어깨를 냅다 쳤어요.
examples.en: That person whacked my shoulder without saying a word.

explain: 힘차고 거칠게, 망설임 없이 갑자기 하는 행동에 써요. '걷어차다, 던지다, 뛰다, 지르다' 같은 동작 동사와 잘 어울리고, 말할 때 생생한 느낌을 줘요.

phrases.en: I was angry, so I flung my bag hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 망설임 없이 거칠게 던지는 모습을 보여 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows throwing something roughly and without hesitation.

phrases.example: 갑자기 누가 냅다 소리를 질러서 놀랐어요.
phrases.en: Someone suddenly yelled at the top of their voice, and I was startled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 갑자기 크게 소리치는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for suddenly shouting loudly.

phrases.example: 버스를 놓칠까 봐 정류장까지 냅다 달렸어요.
phrases.en: I was afraid of missing the bus, so I dashed all the way to the stop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘껏 빠르게 달리는 모습을 생생하게 말해 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Vividly describes running fast with all one's strength.

explain_en: It describes an action done forcefully, roughly and suddenly without hesitation. It goes well with action verbs like '걷어차다', '던지다', '뛰다' and '지르다', and gives a vivid feel in speech.

examples.en: The children dashed across the playground.
I ran as fast as I could for fear of missing the bus.
My friend who is quick on his feet came in first.
The puppy saw its owner and came running.
My younger brother is confident in running.
I heard loud running footsteps in the hallway.

explain: '달리기'보다 옛 느낌이 있고 글이나 이야기에서 더 자주 보여요. 일상 대화에서는 '뛰어가다', '달려가다'를 많이 써요.

phrases.en: The child ran all the way home.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 달음박질에 '하다'를 붙여 동작으로 말하는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adds '하다' to the noun to make it an action.

phrases.en: I ran over when I saw my friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 달음박질 대신 많이 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common everyday alternative to 달음박질.

phrases.en: I was late, so I ran to school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 달음박질보다 가볍고 흔한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Lighter and more common than 달음박질.

explain_en: It feels more old-fashioned than '달리기' and shows up more in writing and stories. In everyday conversation people usually say '뛰어가다' or '달려가다'.

examples.en: I got angry and hurled my bag onto the floor.

examples.ko: 그는 들고 있던 책을 동댕이치고 나가 버렸어요.
examples.en: He flung down the book he was holding and walked out.
If you hurl your phone, it will break.
The child threw the toy down and it broke.
He dropped his luggage as if throwing it and left.
Please don't throw things like that.

explain: '던지다'는 보통 던지는 행동 자체를 말하지만, '동댕이치다'는 화가 나거나 거칠게 힘을 줘서 내던지는 느낌이 있어요. '내동댕이치다'라고도 말하는데 뜻이 같아요.

phrases.example: 화가 난 그는 모자를 땅에 내동댕이쳤어요.
phrases.en: In anger, he flung his hat onto the ground.
phrases.nuance_ko: '동댕이치다'와 뜻이 같고 '내-'가 붙어 더 세게 내던지는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '동댕이치다', with '내-' giving a harder, flinging feeling.

phrases.en: Please don't hurl your toys onto the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거칠게 던지지 말라고 부탁하거나 말릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask or tell someone not to throw things roughly.

phrases.en: He hurled the cup onto the floor and it broke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 던진 곳을 앞에 두고 말하면 장면이 잘 그려져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting the place first makes the scene easy to picture.

explain_en: '던지다' usually just describes the act of throwing, but '동댕이치다' has the feel of flinging something roughly, often out of anger. You can also say '내동댕이치다' with the same meaning.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 아무 말 없이 뒤돌아서 가 버렸어요.
examples.en: He turned around and left without saying a word.
When I called her name, the girl turned around.

examples.ko: 몇 걸음 가다가 다시 뒤돌아서서 손을 흔들었어요.
examples.en: After a few steps, he turned around again and waved.

examples.ko: 화가 나서 뒤돌아서는 모습이 아직 기억나요.
examples.en: I still remember him turning away in anger.
I forget it the moment I turn away.
The moment I turned around, our eyes met.

explain: '뒤돌아보다'는 고개나 눈을 뒤로 돌려 보는 거고, '뒤돌아서다'는 몸 전체를 돌려 서는 거예요. 그래서 헤어지거나 화가 나서 떠나는 장면에 자주 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '돌아서다'도 있어요.

phrases.example: 화가 나서 말도 없이 돌아서 나갔어요.
phrases.en: He got angry and turned and left without a word.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뒤돌아서다'와 비슷하지만, 마음이 떠나거나 관계를 끊는다는 뜻으로도 써서 더 넓게 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 뒤돌아서다 but used more broadly, also for turning away emotionally or cutting ties.

phrases.en: He said goodbye, turned around, and left.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸을 돌린 뒤에 이어서 가는 동작을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the action of walking off after turning around.

phrases.en: Even if I memorize new words, I forget them the moment I turn away.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바로 그다음에'라는 뜻의 비유로, 금방 잊을 때 자주 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative phrase meaning 'right afterward,' used when you forget quickly.

explain_en: '뒤돌아보다' means turning your head or eyes to look back, while '뒤돌아서다' means turning your whole body around. It often appears in scenes of parting or leaving in anger. '돌아서다' is a similar word.

examples.en: The ball rolled down the hill.

examples.ko: 배가 너무 아파서 바닥에서 떼굴떼굴 굴렀어요.
examples.en: My stomach hurt so much that I rolled around on the floor.

examples.ko: 아이가 침대 위에서 떼굴떼굴 구르며 놀아요.
examples.en: The child plays rolling around on the bed.
A chestnut fell on the floor and rolled away.
It was so funny that I almost rolled on the floor laughing.
On Sunday I just lazed around on the sofa.

explain: 물건이 굴러가는 모양에도, 사람이 아파서 또는 웃겨서 구르는 모습에도 써요. '구르다', '뒹굴다'와 같이 쓰는 경우가 많고, 비슷한 '데굴데굴'도 있어요.

phrases.en: The ball rolled away.
phrases.nuance_ko: '떼굴떼굴'과 뜻이 비슷하고 조금 더 가벼운 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '떼굴떼굴', with a slightly lighter feel.

phrases.en: My stomach hurt so much that I rolled around on the floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아픔을 참지 못해 몸을 이리저리 뒹구는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes writhing and rolling around because of unbearable pain.

phrases.en: It was so funny that I rolled on the floor laughing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크게 웃는 모습을 과장해서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to exaggerate laughing very hard.

explain_en: It describes both objects rolling and people rolling around in pain, laughter or laziness. It is usually paired with '구르다' or '뒹굴다', and there is a similar word '데굴데굴'.

examples.en: He struggled desperately to survive.

examples.ko: 아기가 자는 동안 몸부림이 심해서 이불이 다 벗겨졌어요.
examples.en: The baby tossed and turned so much in its sleep that the blanket came off.
Even the last struggle to save the company was useless.

examples.ko: 동생은 잘 때 몸부림쳐서 침대에서 떨어지기도 해요.
examples.en: My younger sibling thrashes around in sleep and sometimes falls off the bed.

examples.ko: 이건 변화에 적응하려는 작은 몸부림일 뿐이에요.
examples.en: This is just a small struggle to adapt to the change.

examples.ko: 그 노력은 몸부림에 가까웠지만 결과는 좋았어요.
examples.en: That effort was close to flailing, but the result was good.

explain: '몸부림을 치다'가 가장 흔한 짝이고, '몸부림치다'처럼 한 단어로도 써요. 몸을 뒤틀며 버둥대는 모습뿐 아니라 어려운 처지에서 벗어나려고 애쓰는 모습에도 써요. 비슷한 '발버둥'도 같은 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: The child was in pain and thrashed around on the bed.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몸부림을 치다'를 한 단어로 붙여 쓴 동사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb that joins '몸부림을 치다' into one word.

phrases.example: 물에 빠진 강아지가 살려고 발버둥 쳤어요.
phrases.en: The puppy that fell into the water struggled to survive.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몸부림'과 비슷하게 벗어나려고 애쓰는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Like 몸부림, it describes struggling to break free.

phrases.en: That was a desperate struggle to escape poverty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어려운 처지에서 벗어나려는 간절한 노력을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an earnest effort to escape a difficult situation.

explain_en: The most common pairing is '몸부림을 치다', and '몸부림치다' is also used as a single verb. It describes literally thrashing the body, and also struggling to escape a hard situation. '발버둥' has a similar feel.

examples.ko: 고양이는 미동도 없이 새를 지켜보고 있었어요.
examples.en: The cat was watching the bird without moving a muscle.

examples.ko: 아기가 깰까 봐 미동조차 하지 않고 가만히 있었어요.
examples.en: I stayed still without even stirring, afraid the baby would wake up.

examples.ko: 문 앞의 남자는 미동 없이 서서 저를 쳐다봤어요.
examples.en: The man at the door stood motionless and stared at me.
No matter how much I called, he didn't budge.

examples.ko: 시험장이 너무 조용해서 아무도 미동도 하지 못했어요.
examples.en: The exam room was so quiet that nobody could move an inch.

examples.ko: 미동 하나 없는 호수 위로 달이 떠 있었어요.
examples.en: The moon hung over the lake, which was perfectly still.

explain: '미동도 없다', '미동도 하지 않다'처럼 부정하는 말과 함께 써서 몸이 조금도 움직이지 않는 모습을 나타내요. 일상 대화에서는 '꼼짝도 안 하다'가 더 자연스러워요. 사람뿐 아니라 동물이나 호수, 물건에도 쓸 수 있어요.

phrases.en: The lake was calm without a single ripple.
phrases.nuance_ko: '없이'와 함께 써서 조금도 움직이지 않는 상태를 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '없이' to show something stays completely still.

phrases.example: 그는 큰 소리가 나도 미동조차 하지 않았어요.
phrases.en: He didn't even budge at the loud noise.
phrases.nuance_ko: '조차'로 '이 정도에도 움직이지 않는다'는 느낌을 더해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '조차' adds the sense of not moving even at something like that.

phrases.en: The puppy isn't moving at all, maybe because it's asleep.
phrases.nuance_ko: '미동'보다 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural in everyday conversation than '미동'.

explain_en: It is typically used with negatives, as in '미동도 없다' or '미동도 하지 않다', to show that something does not move at all. In daily conversation '꼼짝도 안 하다' sounds more natural. It can describe people, animals, or even a lake or an object.

examples.en: My younger sibling pushed me out the door.

examples.ko: 새 건물이 옛 가게를 밀어내고 들어섰어요.
examples.en: A new building pushed out the old shop and took its place.
I pushed the hot pot aside and sat down.
The baby keeps pushing the spoon out of its mouth.

examples.ko: 약한 사람을 밀어내는 건 좋지 않아요.
examples.en: It is not good to push weaker people aside.
The wind pushed the clouds far away.

explain: '밀다'는 힘을 줘서 움직이는 동작 전체이고, '밀어내다'는 밀어서 어떤 자리에서 없애거나 쫓아내는 느낌이 강해요. '밀치다'는 한 번 확 미는 동작이라 달라요. 경쟁에서 누군가의 자리를 빼앗는다는 비유로도 써요.

phrases.en: I pushed the cat out the door.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 곳에서 밖으로 보낼 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for pushing something out of a place.

phrases.en: Please don't push your friend away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁이나 주의를 줄 때 쓰는 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request or warning form.

phrases.en: He pushed aside his rival and became first.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경쟁에서 다른 사람의 자리를 차지한다는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative use for taking someone's place in competition.

explain_en: '밀다' is any pushing motion; '밀어내다' pushes something away from its place, with a feel of removing or driving out. '밀치다' is a single sharp shove. It can also mean taking someone's spot in a competition.

examples.ko: 그는 문을 확 밀어젖히고 안으로 들어갔어요.
examples.en: He pushed the door wide open and went inside.
The wind pushed the window open, and the room got cold.

examples.ko: 사람들을 밀어젖히며 앞으로 나가면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't shove people aside to get to the front.
When I pushed the curtain aside, sunlight poured in.

examples.ko: 문이 안 열려서 어깨로 밀어젖혀 봤어요.
examples.en: The door wouldn't open, so I tried pushing it open with my shoulder.
The person who shoved me aside apologized right away.

explain: 문이나 커튼, 사람을 밀어서 열거나 한쪽으로 치울 때 써요. '밀치다'는 세게 미는 동작 자체를 말하고, '밀어젖히다'는 그래서 열리거나 비켜나는 결과까지 들어 있어요. 동작이 크고 거친 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: When I pushed the curtains aside in the morning, sunlight poured in.
phrases.nuance_ko: 커튼처럼 가리는 것을 힘 있게 한쪽으로 치울 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this for forcefully pushing aside something that covers, like a curtain.

phrases.en: He pushed through the people and went to the front.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세게 미는 동작 자체를 말하고, 열리거나 비켜나는 결과까지 뜻하지는 않아요.
phrases.nuance_en: This describes the pushing motion itself, without implying that something opens or moves away.

phrases.en: Please push the door to open it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거칠지 않게 평범하게 문을 여는 방법을 말하는 쉬운 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a plain, gentle way to describe opening a door by pushing it.

explain_en: It is used when you push a door, curtain or person to open it or move it aside. '밀치다' is the forceful push itself, while '밀어젖히다' also includes the result of something opening or moving out of the way. The motion feels big and rough.

examples.ko: 동생은 자기 말이 맞다고 바득바득 우겨요.
examples.en: My younger brother stubbornly insists he is right.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 바득바득 돈을 받아 내겠다고 했어요.
examples.en: He said he would get the money back no matter what.
The child keeps pestering me to buy it.
Why are you so determined to win at all costs?

examples.ko: 제가 오지 말라고 했는데 친구가 바득바득 따라왔어요.
examples.en: I told my friend not to come, but he insisted on following me.

examples.ko: 바득바득 고집을 부려 봤자 달라지는 건 없어요.
examples.en: Stubbornly digging in your heels won't change anything.

explain: '우기다, 조르다, 고집을 부리다'처럼 끈질기게 밀어붙이는 말과 자주 써요. '악착같이'는 열심히 해내는 느낌으로도 쓰지만, '바득바득'은 억지를 부린다는 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.en: He insists stubbornly even though he's wrong.
phrases.nuance_ko: '바득바득'과 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with 바득바득.

phrases.example: 아이가 장난감을 사 달라고 바득바득 졸라요.
phrases.en: The child keeps pestering me to buy the toy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원하는 것을 얻으려고 끈질기게 부탁하는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes persistently begging to get what one wants.

phrases.en: I saved money tenaciously and bought a house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끈질기게 해내는 점은 비슷하지만 '악착같이'는 열심히 한다는 긍정적인 느낌도 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in persistence, but 악착같이 can also feel positive, like working hard.

explain_en: It pairs with words for pushing persistently, such as '우기다', '조르다' and '고집을 부리다'. '악착같이' can sound like admirable determination, but '바득바득' leans toward being unreasonably stubborn.

en: to wander about; to lose one's way; to stray about

examples.en: After graduating, I drifted aimlessly for a while.
I lost my way and wandered around the alley.
It's a novel about wandering youth.
I'm struggling a lot over my career path.

examples.ko: 너무 오래 방황하지 말고 방향을 정해요.
examples.en: Don't wander for too long, and decide on a direction.
He, who had been drifting, finally found his dream.

explain: 길을 잃고 헤매는 모습도 말하지만, 요즘은 인생 방향을 못 찾고 마음이 흔들리는 시기에 더 자주 써요. '방황의 시기', '방황을 끝내다'처럼 시기와 같이 나와요. 단순히 길을 헤맬 때는 '헤매다'가 더 일상적이에요.

phrases.en: People say your twenties are a time of wandering.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인생의 방향을 찾지 못하고 흔들리는 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to a period of uncertainty about life's direction.

phrases.example: 그는 긴 방황을 끝내고 꿈을 찾았어요.
phrases.en: He ended his long period of wandering and found his dream.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흔들리던 시기가 지나고 마음을 잡는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone settles down after a time of drifting.

phrases.en: I didn't know the way and wandered around for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 길을 찾지 못할 때는 '방황하다'보다 이 말을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For being lost on the road, this is more common than 방황하다.

explain_en: It can mean losing your way physically, but today it is used more for a period of feeling lost about your life direction, as in 방황의 시기. For simply getting lost on the road, 헤매다 is more everyday.

en: to fling off; to throw away

examples.en: As soon as I got home, I flung off my coat.
It's so hot that I want to throw off my coat.
Now try to shake off your old prejudices.
The child kicked off his shoes and ran to the sea.

examples.ko: 그는 체면을 벗어던진 채 춤을 췄어요.
examples.en: He cast aside his dignity and danced.
Don't just fling your socks off; put them in the laundry basket.

explain: 옷이나 신발을 거칠게 벗어 던질 때도 쓰고, 편견·체면·걱정 같은 추상적인 것을 떨쳐 버릴 때도 써요. 그냥 '벗다'보다 힘 있고 시원한 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: I kicked off my shoes and lay down on the sofa.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물건을 거칠게 벗어서 던지듯 둘 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when roughly taking something off and tossing it aside.

phrases.en: If you throw off your prejudice, you'll make more friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나쁜 생각을 완전히 버린다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to completely cast off a bad way of thinking.

phrases.en: Throw off your worries and enjoy your trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 마음의 부담을 시원하게 떨쳐 버릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for shaking off a mental burden with a sense of relief.

explain_en: It is used for taking off clothes or shoes roughly and tossing them aside, and also for shaking off abstract things such as prejudice, dignity or worries. It feels more forceful and liberating than plain '벗다'.

examples.en: I took leave to take care of my mother during her illness.

examples.ko: 며칠째 병간호를 하느라 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I haven't slept for days because I've been nursing someone.
Nursing a patient is hard on the family.
My father was hospitalized, so my older sister took charge of his care.

examples.ko: 병간호에 지친 가족을 위해 간병인을 구했어요.
examples.en: We hired a caregiver for the family worn out from nursing.
After a long period of nursing, my grandmother recovered.

explain: '병간호를 하다/맡다'처럼 써요. 가족이 아픈 사람을 곁에서 돌보는 일에 많이 쓰고, 직업으로 하는 사람은 '간병인'이라고 해요. 동사로는 '간호하다'나 '돌보다'도 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: My older brother is in charge of caring for our mother.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누가 그 일을 책임지는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say who takes responsibility for the care.

phrases.en: I took care of my sick child all night.
phrases.nuance_ko: '병간호'와 뜻이 가까운 동사예요. 아픈 사람을 곁에서 돌본다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A verb close in meaning to 병간호: to look after a sick person at their side.

phrases.en: We hired a caregiver at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병간호를 직업으로 하는 사람을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A person who does nursing care as a job.

explain_en: It is used as '병간호를 하다/맡다', most often for family members looking after a sick person. A professional who does this is called a '간병인'. As verbs, '간호하다' and '돌보다' are also common.

en: to support someone by the arm; to help someone walk

examples.en: I supported Grandma at her side so she wouldn't fall.

examples.ko: 다리를 다친 친구를 부축해서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: I supported my friend, who hurt his leg, and we went to the hospital.
Please help the elderly person on the stairs.
He walked while supporting his stumbling father.
I'll support you, so please get up slowly.

examples.ko: 아픈 동생을 부축하는 모습이 보기 좋았어요.
examples.en: It was nice to see him supporting his sick younger sibling.

explain: 몸이 불편한 사람의 팔이나 몸을 잡고 걷거나 일어나게 도울 때 써서, 그냥 '돕다'보다 동작이 구체적이에요. 어르신께는 '부축해 드리다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I helped my grandfather by supporting his arm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어르신께 쓰는 높임 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Honorific form for elders.

phrases.en: My father walked with my support.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도움을 받는 사람 쪽에서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said from the point of view of the person helped.

phrases.en: I helped the fallen child up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 넘어진 사람을 일으킬 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for helping a fallen person up.

explain_en: It is used when you hold someone's arm or body so they can walk or stand, which makes it more physical than plain '돕다'. For an elder, say '부축해 드리다'.

dis.h: hold someone's arm to steady them

p.n: The replacement is vague and does not mean physically holding her arm.

examples.ko: 열이 나서 비틀비틀 걸어 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: I had a fever, so I staggered to the hospital.

examples.ko: 아기가 비틀비틀 걷다가 엄마 품에 안겼어요.
examples.en: The baby toddled unsteadily and fell into its mom's arms.

examples.ko: 너무 피곤해서 비틀비틀하며 겨우 집에 왔어요.
examples.en: I was so tired that I stumbled along and barely made it home.
He rose unsteadily and then sat back down.
The ship was rocking, so people walked unsteadily.

examples.ko: 자전거를 처음 탈 때는 비틀비틀 흔들려요.
examples.en: When you first ride a bike, you wobble from side to side.

explain: 몸이 힘이 없거나 균형을 잃어서 이리저리 흔들리는 모습에 써요. 동사 '비틀거리다'와 함께 외우면 좋고, 뒤에 '걷다, 일어서다' 같은 말이 자주 와요.

phrases.en: A drunk person is walking while staggering.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비틀비틀'과 짝을 이루는 동사로, 실제 흔들리는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb that pairs with '비틀비틀', describing the actual swaying movement.

phrases.en: I was so tired that I walked unsteadily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘이 없어서 균형을 잃은 걸음걸이에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an unbalanced gait due to weakness.

phrases.en: I fell and then got up unsteadily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일어서는 순간 몸이 흔들리는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows the body wobbling at the moment of standing up.

explain_en: It describes a body swaying back and forth when weak or off balance. It is good to learn it with the verb '비틀거리다', and it is often followed by words like '걷다' (walk) and '일어서다' (stand up).

examples.en: The plan went rocky from the start, so I was worried.
I can hear the old door creaking.
The teamwork is shaky.
The bed creaked all night.

examples.ko: 마루가 삐걱댈 때마다 할아버지 생각이 나요.
examples.en: Every time the floor creaks, I think of my grandfather.

examples.ko: 일이 삐걱대도 포기하지 말고 다시 해 봐요.
examples.en: Even if things go rocky, don't give up and try again.

explain: 문이나 마루가 내는 소리에도 쓰고, 일이나 사이가 순조롭지 않을 때 비유로도 많이 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '삐걱거리다'도 써요.

phrases.example: 결혼 후 부부 사이가 삐걱대기 시작했어요.
phrases.en: The relationship starts to creak.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 사람이나 조직의 관계가 순조롭지 않고 서로 맞지 않는 상태를 소리에 빗대어 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It compares a strained relationship between people or within a group to a creaking sound, meaning things are not running smoothly.

explain_en: It is used for the sound of doors or floors, and also figuratively when work or a relationship is not going smoothly. '삐걱거리다' is also used with the same meaning.

examples.en: It snowed a lot, so I've been shoveling since morning.
I'm digging with a shovel to plant potatoes in the garden.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 삽질해서 손에 물집이 생겼어요.
examples.en: I shoveled all day, so I got blisters on my hands.

examples.ko: 설명서도 안 보고 하다가 괜히 삽질했네요.
examples.en: I didn't read the manual and ended up wasting effort for nothing.

examples.ko: 또 삽질하기 싫으면 처음부터 자료를 꼼꼼히 확인하세요.
examples.en: If you don't want to waste effort again, check the materials carefully from the start.

examples.ko: 방법을 몰라서 혼자 삽질하다가 결국 선배한테 물어봤어요.
examples.en: I didn't know how, so after flailing around alone I finally asked my senior.

explain: 원래는 삽으로 땅을 파거나 눈을 치우는 일이지만, 요즘 입말에서는 방법을 몰라서 헛수고를 하거나 쓸데없이 시간을 낭비했을 때도 써요. 친구끼리 가볍게 쓰는 말이라 윗사람에게는 '헛수고하다'가 더 안전해요.

phrases.en: I dug the ground with a shovel and planted a tree.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 뜻을 풀어서 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase that spells out the original meaning of shoveling.

phrases.en: I cleared snow in front of the apartment this morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 삽으로 눈을 치우는 일을 가리킬 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for clearing snow with a shovel.

phrases.en: I didn't read the instructions, so it was all wasted effort.
phrases.nuance_ko: '삽질하다'의 헛수고 뜻과 같지만 윗사람에게도 쓸 수 있는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same as the 'wasted effort' sense of '삽질하다', but safe to use with superiors.

explain_en: Literally it means digging the ground or clearing snow with a shovel, but in today's spoken Korean it is also used when you waste effort or time because you didn't know the right way. It is casual talk among friends, so '헛수고하다' is safer with someone senior.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감을 사 달라고 생떼를 써요.
examples.en: The child throws a tantrum, demanding I buy the toy.

examples.ko: 생떼 쓰지 말고 이유를 말해 보세요.
examples.en: Don't be unreasonable; tell me your reason.

examples.ko: 생떼에 못 이겨 결국 사 줬어요.
examples.en: I couldn't stand the nagging and ended up buying it for him.

examples.ko: 동생의 생떼가 시작되면 아무도 못 말려요.
examples.en: Once my younger sibling starts being stubborn, nobody can stop it.
He insists unreasonably, but he has no evidence.

examples.ko: 그렇게 생떼만 부리면 아무도 도와주지 않아요.
examples.en: If you only act unreasonably like that, nobody will help you.

explain: '생떼를 쓰다/부리다'로 짝지어 쓰고, 안 되는 일을 막무가내로 조르거나 우길 때 말해요. '떼를 쓰다'보다 억지스러운 느낌이 더 강하고, 아이뿐 아니라 어른에게도 써요.

phrases.example: 아이가 과자를 사 달라고 생떼를 써요.
phrases.en: The child insists unreasonably that I buy snacks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 대표적인 짝말이에요. 안 되는 일을 계속 우길 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most typical pairing, for stubbornly insisting on something impossible.

phrases.example: 동생이 게임을 더 하겠다고 생떼를 부려요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling insists unreasonably on playing more games.
phrases.nuance_ko: '생떼를 쓰다'와 뜻이 같고 서로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '생떼를 쓰다' and interchangeable with it.

phrases.en: Please don't make unreasonable demands here.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른에게도 쓸 수 있지만 꽤 직접적인 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Can be said to adults too, but it is quite direct.

explain_en: It pairs with '쓰다' or '부리다' as '생떼를 쓰다/부리다', for insisting or begging stubbornly for something impossible. It feels more unreasonable than '떼를 쓰다' and can be used for adults as well as children.

examples.ko: 동료가 아무 이유 없이 제 보고서에 생트집을 잡아요.
examples.en: My coworker finds fault with my report for no reason at all.
It is hard to work with someone who only picks petty quarrels.

examples.ko: 이건 생트집 아니에요? 저는 잘못한 게 없어요.
examples.en: Isn't this just nitpicking? I did nothing wrong.
He tried to break the contract on a groundless pretext.
Don't respond to every one of those groundless complaints.

examples.ko: 그 말은 생트집이라서 신경 쓰지 않기로 했어요.
examples.en: That comment was just nitpicking, so I decided to ignore it.

explain: '트집'에 비해 이유 없이 억지를 부리는 느낌이 강해요. 보통 '생트집을 잡다'나 '생트집을 부리다'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 상사가 이유 없이 제 일에 생트집을 잡아요.
phrases.en: My boss finds fault with my work for no reason.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말이에요. 억지로 흠을 찾아 따질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for forcing a complaint out of nothing.

phrases.en: That customer kept making groundless complaints.
phrases.nuance_ko: '잡다'보다 억지로 계속 우기는 느낌이 더 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Feels more like stubbornly keeping it up than '잡다'.

phrases.en: That's just unreasonable nitpicking.
phrases.nuance_ko: 누군가의 불평이 억지라고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone's complaint is unreasonable.

explain_en: Compared with '트집' (fault-finding), it has a stronger sense of making a groundless, forced complaint. It usually appears as '생트집을 잡다' or '생트집을 부리다'.

examples.ko: 약속 시간보다 일찍 와서 역 앞에서 서성댔어요.
examples.en: I arrived earlier than planned and hung around in front of the station.

examples.ko: 아이가 교문 앞에서 서성대는 걸 보고 말을 걸었어요.
examples.en: I saw a child lingering in front of the school gate and spoke to him.

examples.ko: 면접 전에 긴장돼서 복도를 서성대고 있었어요.
examples.en: I was nervous before the interview, so I was pacing the hallway.

examples.ko: 누가 집 앞에서 서성대서 좀 무서웠어요.
examples.en: Someone was loitering in front of my house, and it was a little scary.
Don't just hover there, come in and have a seat.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 병원 앞을 서성댄 사람은 그의 아버지였어요.
examples.en: The person who paced in front of the hospital all day was his father.

explain: '서성이다'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요. 기다리거나 망설이며 한 곳 주변을 왔다 갔다 할 때 써요. 걷는 것이 목적인 '산책하다'와 달리 불안, 기다림, 망설임의 느낌이 있어요.

phrases.en: He lingered in front of the door for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '서성대다'와 같은 뜻이고 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 서성대다, and used more often.

phrases.en: After hanging around for a while, I went inside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-다가'로 서성이던 동작 다음에 다른 일이 이어져요.
phrases.nuance_en: -다가 connects the pacing to the action that follows.

phrases.en: Don't hang around outside, come in.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-지 말고'로 그만하고 다른 행동을 하라고 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: -지 말고 tells someone to stop and do something else.

explain_en: It is used with the same meaning as '서성이다'. It is for moving back and forth around one spot while waiting or hesitating. Unlike '산책하다', where walking is the point, it carries a feeling of anxiety, waiting or indecision.

en: to clean up; to handle; to put in order; to collect (scattered things)

examples.ko: 사고가 나자 직원들이 서둘러 상황을 수습했어요.
examples.en: After the accident, the staff hurried to sort out the situation.
I made the mistake, so I'll clean it up myself.
The team leader stepped in to settle the fight.
I gathered up the scattered things and put them in my bag.

examples.ko: 문제가 커지기 전에 빨리 수습해야 해요.
examples.en: We have to handle the problem fast before it gets bigger.

examples.ko: 사장님이 사과문을 올리고 사태를 수습하고 있어요.
examples.en: The boss posted an apology and is dealing with the incident.

explain: 수습하다는 어지럽고 문제가 생긴 상황을 정리해서 바로잡는다는 느낌이에요. 사고, 실수, 싸움처럼 일이 꼬였을 때 자주 쓰고, 흩어진 물건을 모을 때도 써요. 일이 커지기 전에 마무리한다는 뜻이라 '사태를 수습하다'가 뉴스에 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The team leader stepped up first and sorted out the situation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문제가 생긴 상황을 바로잡는다는 뜻의 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, meaning to set a troubled situation right.

phrases.example: 일이 너무 커져서 수습할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: Things have grown too big to be put right.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄹ 수 없다'를 붙이면 이미 너무 꼬여서 바로잡기 어렵다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '-ㄹ 수 없다' it means things are already too tangled to fix.

phrases.en: I hurriedly gathered up the papers blown away by the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여기저기 흩어진 것을 모아 정리할 때도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used for collecting and tidying things scattered around.

explain_en: 수습하다 carries the feel of tidying up and fixing a messy or troubled situation. It is common after accidents, mistakes, or fights, and also for gathering scattered things. '사태를 수습하다' (bring a situation under control) appears often in the news.

examples.en: A pickpocket suddenly snatched my bag.
When I jerked the fishing rod, a big fish came up.

examples.ko: 그는 내 손목을 잡아채서 밖으로 끌고 갔어요.
examples.en: He grabbed my wrist and pulled me outside.
A motorcycle came closer to snatch the bag.
Please don't take things as if you're snatching them.
The person who snatched the wallet ran away.

explain: 갑자기 힘을 주어 확 잡아당겨 가지는 동작이에요. 가방 날치기나 낚시에서 자주 나오고, '낚아채다'와 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.en: The child snatched the snack out of my hand.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 거의 같은 말이고, 빠르게 가로채는 느낌이 더 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Nearly the same meaning, with more of a quick-grab feeling.

phrases.en: I was startled when someone suddenly yanked my wrist.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동작을 이어서 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connecting form for describing the next action or result.

phrases.en: Please don't suddenly yank my arm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거친 행동을 하지 말라고 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask someone not to grab roughly.

explain_en: It describes grabbing something and yanking it suddenly with force. It often appears in bag-snatching and fishing contexts, and is used much like '낚아채다'.

examples.en: Try wringing out the wet towel tightly.
I squeezed a lemon into the water.

examples.ko: 아무리 머리를 쥐어짜도 생각이 안 나요.
examples.en: No matter how hard I rack my brain, I can't remember.
If you wring out the laundry, a lot of water comes out.
The toothpaste was almost gone, so I squeezed out every last bit.
It hurt as if my heart were being wrung.

explain: '짜다'보다 손에 힘을 더 줘서 꽉 쥐고 누르는 느낌이에요. 수건이나 레몬 같은 물건에도 쓰고, '머리를 쥐어짜다'처럼 애써서 생각을 짜낼 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 머리를 쥐어짜서 겨우 아이디어를 하나 냈어요.
phrases.en: rack one's brain
phrases.nuance_ko: 방법이 안 떠오를 때 애써서 열심히 생각하는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes thinking very hard when no idea comes easily.

explain_en: Compared with 짜다, it feels like gripping and pressing harder with your hand. It is used for towels and lemons, and also for forcing out ideas, as in '머리를 쥐어짜다'.

examples.en: My friend gave me a telling-off for coming late.
How could you scold me first instead of helping?

examples.ko: 작은 실수에도 핀잔이 돌아와서 기분이 상했어요.
examples.en: Even a small mistake got me a rebuke, and it upset me.

examples.ko: 핀잔 섞인 말투 때문에 마음이 불편했어요.
examples.en: His scolding tone made me uncomfortable.
He answered with a smile even when he was rebuked.
I spoke up for no reason and just got told off.

explain: '핀잔을 주다'(하는 쪽)와 '핀잔을 듣다/먹다'(받는 쪽)를 짝으로 외워 두세요. '꾸중'이 윗사람이 크게 혼내는 느낌이라면, '핀잔'은 면박을 주듯 가볍게 말하는 느낌에 가까워요.

phrases.en: When his younger brother made a mistake, his older brother scolded him.
phrases.nuance_ko: 핀잔을 하는 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person doing the telling-off.

phrases.en: I got told off for being late to the appointment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 핀잔을 받는 쪽에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person receiving the rebuke.

phrases.example: 숙제를 안 해서 선생님께 핀잔을 먹었어요.
phrases.en: I got scolded by my teacher for not doing my homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: '핀잔을 듣다'와 뜻은 같지만 더 구어체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 핀잔을 듣다 but more colloquial.

explain_en: Learn '핀잔을 주다' (to give it) and '핀잔을 듣다/먹다' (to receive it) as a pair. While '꾸중' feels like an elder scolding someone seriously, '핀잔' is closer to a light putdown.
